newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police find body in kidnap probe.
newsitem.headline: German police find body in kidnap probe.

text.p: Police searching for kidnapped Frankfurt businessman Jakub Fiszman, abducted over two weeks ago, said on Saturday they had found a body but could not say immediately if it was that of the missing multi-millionaire.
Tracker dogs discovered the body in countryside in the Taunus region about 50 km (30 miles) from Frankfurt.
"I can confirm we have found a body," a police spokesman said, adding more details would be a given at a news conference at police headquarters in Wiesbaden later in the afternoon.
Two suspects, 48-year-old Rainer Koerppen and his 26-year-old son Sven, have been in custody since Wednesday.
Prosecutors said on Friday the son had confessed to helping with the kidnap and that he and his father had taken Fiszman to the Taunus region a few days after his October 1 abduction.

Sven Koerppen told police his father had made him get out of the car before entering a wooded area and then drove off with Fiszman, prosectors said. The father returned about 30 to 45 minutes later alone, according to his son's testimony.
Police have concentrated their search on the Taunus region since Thursday and called in Tornado reconnaisance jets with heat-seeking equipment on Friday.
Fiszman's brother Georg paid a ransom of four million marks ($2.6 million) on October 10, but his kidnappers reneged on an agreement and failed to free him the following day.
The only sign of life from Fiszman since he was abducted outside his Frankfurt office has been a telephone call the next day to a woman friend to say he was being held in a cellar.
Police said on Friday they were becoming more pessimistic abou the fate of the 40-year-old businessman, whose family's fortune has been put at over 400 million marks ($260 million).
Police recovered most of the ransom on Wednesday in the garden of an apartment in Wiesbaden owned by Rainer Koerppen's parents.
They originally detained five people in connection with the kidnapping but three have since been released. They are still looking for at least one other person.
Prosecutors have said police are reviewing whether there could be any connection between the abduction of Fiszman and that of his nephew in 1991.
The nephew, who was six years old at the time, was released three days later. Media reports have said the family paid one million marks ransom after he was released.
Fiszman, reputed to be one of the richest men in Frankfurt, has widespread property interests and an electronic retailing business.
He has recently hit the headlines for financing an ambitious but the ultimately ill-fated Frankfurt production of the rock musical "Tommy".
